Hi Sanjay / Meera —

Great speaking earlier — quick recap + a couple of asks so we can turn this into a concrete pricing estimate.

Call highlights (my take):
- Volume: you mentioned roughly ~200M tokens / month as a target if things scale.
- Traffic shape: peaks around 20 TPS; most traffic is user prompts + product metadata + a handful of system prompts.
- Reuse: you estimated 60-75% of the traffic has repeated prefixes (system prompts + product descriptions) that look cacheable.
- Budget: you're currently spending a few thousand / month and are evaluating options; you flagged a target effective unit of ~ $600 / 1M tokens as a helpful benchmark for your finance folks.

To run a clean estimate on our side we need two quick items (if you can share):
1) A small sample of usage (anonymized logs) or a CSV of prompt prefixes so we can estimate prefix hit rate — that's the single biggest lever for effective cost.
2) Confirmation of your rough monthly token range (you said ~200M — confirm whether that's monthly active or peak month).

I attached a short outline (redwood-pricing-estimate-acme-20260525.pdf) that shows how we break down raw token cost, caching assumptions, and example effective $/1M under different hit rates.

Next steps I propose:
- If you're comfortable sharing a small sample log, we'll run a hit-rate analysis and produce a concise ROI sheet showing effective $/1M at 40/60/80% hit rates and recommended cache strategy (prefix + KV).
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the numbers and discuss a short pilot.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Sanjay / Meera —

Thanks for the sample logs — we ran a quick analysis and attached a concise estimate (redwood-pricing-estimate-acme-20260530.pdf) plus the model workbook (cache-hit-rate-model.xlsx). Short summary below; happy to walk through on a 30-min call.

Assumptions we used (high level):
- Baseline billable price (model tier): $1,200 per 1M tokens. This is the nominal per-token price at the committed volume band for the chosen model.
- Cache behavior: we assume prefix caching for repeated system prompts/product descriptions. A prefix cache hit avoids re-sending the prompt prefix tokens to the model; in practice the model only processes the variable suffix.
- Effective billed tokens = raw tokens * (1 - cache_hit_rate). For partial hits (only part of the prefix cached), we model partial token savings; the workbook shows that in detail.

Sensitivity (effective $/1M tokens):
- 40% cache hit => effective cost = $1,200 * (1 - 0.40) = $720 / 1M tokens
- 60% cache hit => effective cost = $1,200 * (1 - 0.60) = $480 / 1M tokens
- 80% cache hit => effective cost = $1,200 * (1 - 0.80) = $240 / 1M tokens

Notes on prefix vs KV caching and practical impact:
- Prefix cache (our most effective lever for Acme): when the prefix (system prompt + product metadata) is identical, we can avoid sending those tokens to the model. For Acme, because product descriptions are stable and many requests use the same system prompt, prefix cache hit rates map directly to large token savings.
- KV / response caching: useful when full responses are repeated; fewer wins for your workload unless you have highly templated outputs.
- Partial hits: when only part of the prefix matches, we still save proportional tokens. The workbook models an average prefix length of 40 tokens and average variable suffix of 60 tokens — partial matches reduce billed tokens accordingly.
- Billing model: Redwood bills on tokens processed by the model. Cache hits reduce billed tokens because we avoid re-processing cached prefixes. (We include logging and instrumentation so you can see hit rates in the Console.)

Putting this to your stated target: you mentioned a target effective ~$600 / 1M. That sits between our 40% and 60% hit-rate scenarios. If your real-world hit rate is ~55-65%, you're at or below that $600 target. Our analysis on your sample suggests a realistic prefix hit rate around 60% (see attached workbook), which would put you near $480 / 1M.

Pilot suggestion (low friction):
- 2-week pilot with instrumentation: we enable prefix caching + Console dashboards and run on a small reserved pool. We measure real hit rates and report back a precise effective unit cost. Pilot promo: 30% off list for the pilot period so you can validate economics without commitment.

If that sounds good I can book a 30-min call early next week to walk through the workbook and the pilot logistics.

Best —
